subject: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
title: Mechanics of Materials and Structures — MCQ Practice
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit II scope and existing ACADRIX 1-mark bank. Not official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.q: Stress is defined as:
options: Internal resisting force per unit area
questions.answer: Internal resisting force per unit area
questions.explanation: Stress represents the internal resisting force developed per unit area under loading.

questions.q: The SI unit of stress is:
questions.explanation: Stress is measured in pascals (Pa), equivalent to N/m².

questions.q: Strain is:
questions.explanation: Strain is the deformation produced per unit original dimension.

questions.q: Normal strain is generally:
questions.explanation: Normal strain is a ratio of two lengths and therefore has no dimension.

questions.q: A pulling load acting concentrically on a member primarily produces:
questions.explanation: A concentric axial pulling load produces tensile normal stress in the member.

questions.q: A pushing load acting concentrically on a member primarily produces:
questions.explanation: A concentric axial pushing load produces compressive normal stress.

questions.q: Shear stress acts:
questions.explanation: Shear stress acts tangentially to the area and tends to cause relative sliding.

questions.q: For uniform axial loading, the basic normal-stress relation is:
questions.explanation: Normal stress equals axial load divided by loaded cross-sectional area.

questions.q: Elasticity is the ability of a material to:
options: Regain its original shape within its elastic range after unloading
questions.answer: Regain its original shape within its elastic range after unloading
questions.explanation: Elastic materials tend to recover their original dimensions when load is removed within the elastic range.

questions.q: Plasticity refers to the ability to:
options: Undergo permanent deformation without rupture after exceeding the elastic range
Return instantly to the original shape under any load
questions.answer: Undergo permanent deformation without rupture after exceeding the elastic range
questions.explanation: Plasticity describes permanent deformation after the elastic range has been exceeded without immediate rupture.

questions.q: Strength of a material indicates its ability to:
questions.explanation: Strength describes the ability of a material to withstand applied loading without failure.

questions.q: Toughness is most closely associated with a material's ability to:
options: Absorb energy and plastically deform before fracture
questions.answer: Absorb energy and plastically deform before fracture
questions.explanation: Toughness represents the capacity to absorb energy and undergo plastic deformation before fracture.

questions.q: Hardness is the resistance to:
options: Localized permanent deformation such as indentation
questions.answer: Localized permanent deformation such as indentation
questions.explanation: Hardness commonly describes resistance to indentation, scratching and localized deformation.

questions.q: Axial loading means that the applied force acts:
options: Perpendicular to the member's longitudinal axis
Only tangentially to a circular surface
questions.explanation: Axial loading acts along the longitudinal axis of the member.

questions.q: Bending of a member is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: Bending effects produce curvature and a distribution of normal stresses across the section.

questions.q: Torsion of a member is caused by:
options: An applied torque or twisting moment
questions.answer: An applied torque or twisting moment
questions.explanation: Torsion is twisting caused by an applied torque or twisting moment.

questions.q: A beam is primarily designed to resist:
questions.explanation: A beam is a structural member primarily intended to resist transverse loading and bending.

questions.q: A truss generally carries loads mainly through:
questions.explanation: A truss is made of interconnected members, generally arranged in triangular units, carrying loads mainly through axial forces.

questions.q: In structural analysis, support conditions are important because they determine:
options: The restraints and reactions affecting structural response
Only the density of the material
questions.answer: The restraints and reactions affecting structural response
questions.explanation: Supports impose restraints and create reactions that influence how a structure responds to loading.

questions.q: The SI unit of torque is:
questions.explanation: Torque is a moment of force and is expressed in newton-metres (N·m) in SI.

questions.q: A bending moment represents the:
options: Turning effect of a force about a reference point or section
questions.answer: Turning effect of a force about a reference point or section
questions.explanation: A bending moment is a turning effect associated with bending of a member about a point or section.

questions.q: A safe structural design should consider both strength and deformation because:
options: A component must resist failure and maintain acceptable deformation
Strength applies only to electrical systems
questions.answer: A component must resist failure and maintain acceptable deformation
questions.explanation: Engineering design must satisfy strength requirements while keeping deformation within acceptable functional limits.

questions.q: Which set contains the three basic stress types listed in ME25C03 Unit II?
questions.explanation: The Unit II scope specifically introduces tensile, compressive and shear stress.

questions.q: Which pair represents the two deformation modes specifically introduced besides axial loading?
questions.explanation: Unit II introduces bending and torsion along with axial loading and simple structural analysis.
